doc.title: Clyde Kerr Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006

title: Choosing gigs now; playing jazz in church
summary: Retired, he plays only what fulfils him, prefers churches to noisy clubs, and notes jazz in church was once forbidden.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Like I could spend a week in hell for a three or four hour gig. I want to feel good about playing music. I want to walk away from that feeling fulfilled in some kind of way. That’s what I need to feel to feed my creative spirit. I like playing in church, because playing in church these days, I mean you have an audience that you don’t have people selling drinks, people are not smoking, people are not talking. In a lot of clubs in New Orleans man there’s so much noise in there that it’s hard to concentrate. When I was a young musician and I played in places like that it didn’t matter because I really was trying to play. I was listening and trying to get things together. I’m still trying to play because I won’t ever get to the point where I say I have it all because I know I never will. But I hear the noise now and I hear all the talking. I hear the clatter of glass and drinks, I hear the mixture of the machines making the drinks, so it’s like a slap in the face. When you play in the church you have a captive audience you know. And it’s a great place to play man. And it’s funny because when I was coming up you couldn’t play jazz in church, just jazz in the church. But like within the last ten, fifteen years, I remember once I was playing in the church and I was playing a tune, something I wrote, I said wow, man, I’m playing this music in church you know. I said wow. It just hit me all of a sudden. Times have changed you know. And people appreciate it and why not? Because I offer all my playing to the creator who has given me the talent. That’s the first thing.
